raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MoE padded-row masking constructs row indices with `torch.arange`. Without an
explicit dtype, these indices default to `int64`, while
`num_token_non_padded` may use another integer dtype such as `int32`.

Mixed-dtype tensor comparisons are not supported uniformly across execution
backends and may select an unnecessary fallback path. Constructing row indices
with the token-count tensor's dtype keeps the comparison backend-neutral while
preserving the existing masking semantics.

## Modifications

- Construct padded-row indices with `num_token_non_padded.dtype` throughout
  `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`.
- Preserve the existing ID masking, weight zeroing, fill values, and no-padding
  behavior.
- Add focused regression coverage for `int32` and `int64` token counts.
- Verify the actual comparison operand dtypes while still executing and
  validating the real masking operations.
- Extend non-contiguous eager-fallback coverage for both top-k IDs and weights.


## Accuracy Tests

No model accuracy evaluation was run because this change does not alter routing
or masking results.

Focused test:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python \
  test/registered/moe/test_topk_padded_region.py -v
```

Result: OK — 13 tests discovered, 1 passed locally, and 12 accelerator tests
were skipped because no GPU was available.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. The change only specifies the integer dtype of temporary row indices.
It introduces no additional operations or device synchronization.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+class _ComparisonDtypeRecorder(TorchDispatchMode):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.input_dtypes = []
+
+    def __torch_dispatch__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        if func is torch.ops.aten.ge.Tensor:
+            self.input_dtypes.append((args[0].dtype, args[1].dtype))
+        return func(*args, **(kwargs or {}))
+
+
+class TestTopkPaddedRegionEagerDtype(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_comparison_operands_follow_count_dtype(self):
+        """Mixed integer comparisons can fall back to CPU on accelerators that
+        require matching input dtypes, so every eager mask must use the routing
+        count's dtype while preserving the padded-row result.
+        """
+        cases = (
+            (
+                "ids",
+                torch.full((5, 3), 7, dtype=torch.int32),
+                _mask_topk_ids_padded_region,
+                -1,
+            ),
+            (
+                "weights",
+                torch.full((5, 3), 1.25, dtype=torch.float32),
+                _zero_topk_weights_padded_region,
+                0.0,
+            ),
+        )
+        for count_dtype in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+            for name, source, helper, fill_value in cases:
+                with self.subTest(count_dtype=count_dtype, name=name):
+                    actual = source.clone()
+                    expected = source.clone()
+                    expected[3:] = fill_value
+                    count = torch.tensor(3, dtype=count_dtype)
+                    recorder = _ComparisonDtypeRecorder()
+                    with recorder:
+                        helper(actual, count)
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        recorder.input_dtypes, [(count_dtype, count_dtype)]
+                    )
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual, expected))
+
+
